stories.headline: Trump rules out striking Iran before Nov 3 midterms as Tehran weighs US reply on Hormuz

key_facts.fact: On October 8, Trump posted on Truth Social that the US will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterm elections, calling talks with Tehran 'productive'.
key_facts.excerpt: "I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition … we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on Nov 3," Trump wrote.

key_facts.fact: The pledge came after US outlets reported the Pentagon had drawn up plans to relaunch attacks on Iran before the vote; Axios reported CENTCOM was told to prepare for imminent major combat operations.
key_facts.excerpt: On Wednesday, US publication Axios cited US and Israeli officials saying the Pentagon has instructed US Central Command (CENTCOM) to prepare for imminent major combat operations.

key_facts.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran is still reviewing Washington's response to its seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and could reply within days.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran could reply within days, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency, emphasising that "the diplomatic process is still continuing".

key_facts.fact: Trump said the US naval blockade of Iranian ports will stay in place; Iran's atomic energy chief Mohammad Eslami said Iran will not give up uranium enrichment.
key_facts.excerpt: He also reiterated his claim that Iran has been defeated "economically and militarily" and said the US naval blockade will remain in place ... Iran will not abandon uranium enrichment or hand over its uranium, state media reported Thursday, citing Mohammad Eslami.

key_facts.fact: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains about 75% below pre-conflict levels, per a UKMTO report, and Yemen's Houthis targeted Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport three times on Thursday.
key_facts.excerpt: Yemen's Houthis targeted Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport three times on Thursday ... Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains around 75 per cent below pre-conflict levels

key_facts.fact: Kpler data showed vessel transits through Hormuz fell to seven on Tuesday, the lowest in more than two months, after tanker attacks hit a wartime high.
key_facts.excerpt: shipping data from analytics firm Kpler showed the number of vessels transiting the strait fell to seven on Tuesday, the lowest in more than two months, before edging up to 10 on Wednesday

stories.headline: Brent jumps to ~$106 on tanker attacks and Hurricane Isaias; 30-year Treasury auction tops 5.6%

key_facts.fact: Brent crude hit $105.91 on Thursday morning, 5.7% above Wednesday's close, and still held about 72% of the gain after Trump's no-strike post.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude hit $105.91 Thursday morning, 5.7% above Wednesday's close. At 12:17 p.m. Eastern, President Trump posted ... By 1:45 p.m. Brent was at $104.30, still up 4.1%.

key_facts.fact: Hurricane Isaias, the first of the Atlantic season, forced Gulf of Mexico producers to shut in roughly a quarter of crude output and about 16% of natural gas production.
key_facts.excerpt: Hurricane Isaias, the first of the Atlantic season, forced Gulf of Mexico producers to shut in approximately a quarter of crude oil output and around 16% of natural gas production.

key_facts.fact: The US Treasury sold $22 billion of reopened 30-year bonds at 5.618%, the highest yield at a 30-year auction since August 2000.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury sold $22 billion of reopened 30-year bonds at 5.618%, up from 5.308% in September. That is the highest yield at a 30-year auction since August 2000.

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 5 basis points to 5.35%, near its highest level since 2002, while the S&P 500 slipped about 0.4% and the Russell 2000 fell 1.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: the 10-year Treasury yield rose about 5 basis points to 5.35%, nearing its highest level since 2002 ... The S&P 500 slipped about 0.4% to 7,771 ... The Russell 2000 underperformed, sliding 1.1%

key_facts.fact: In Asia, Japan's Nikkei fell 1.4% and South Korea's Kospi lost 2.6%; Europe's Euro Stoxx 50 dropped 1.1% with banks down nearly 2%.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.4 per cent to 69,042.11 and South Korea's Kospi lost 2.6 per cent to 6,625.93.

key_facts.fact: Bitcoin slid below $81,000, its lowest since September 21, and ether fell about 6.4%; heating oil (diesel) futures rose about 5.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: Bitcoin traded near $80,600 at 1:50 p.m., down about 3% and below $81,000, its lowest since Sept. 21. Ether fell about 6.4% ... Heating oil futures rose about 5.1%

stories.headline: Russian glide bomb kills 30+ on Kramatorsk buses; Kyiv blacked out as Ukraine heads to Miami talks

key_facts.fact: A Russian guided bomb hit a street next to two packed city buses in Kramatorsk on October 8, killing at least 30 people and wounding at least 18, officials said.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 30 people were killed Thursday when a Russian guided bomb slammed into a street near two packed city buses in Kramatorsk, eastern Ukraine ... At least 18 more people were wounded

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said 78 people were killed and 215 wounded by Russian strikes over two days, and accused Washington of 'unwillingness' to help Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskiy said 78 people were killed and 215 wounded by strikes in the last two days across Ukraine ... "That's called unwillingness," he said, referring to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's assertion

key_facts.fact: A Russian attack on an energy facility left most of Kyiv without power, halting the metro and disrupting water supply; Ukrenergo imposed consumption limits for October 9.
key_facts.excerpt: The Russian attack on Ukrainian energy infrastructure on Oct. 8 has caused widespread power outages across the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, home to over 3 million people ... the city metro shut down due to lack of electricity.

key_facts.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he saw no 'clear path' to a peaceful resolution, while Rubio called the war a dangerous stalemate.
key_facts.excerpt: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Thursday in Moscow that he didn't see a "clear path" to any peaceful resolution to the war

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian negotiators are to meet US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Miami on Friday for two days of talks, with Kyiv hoping European partners join.
key_facts.excerpt: The remarks came as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner prepare to meet Ukrainian officials in Miami on Friday in a fresh attempt to revive efforts to end the war.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine said it struck the Salavat refinery and petrochemical complex in Bashkortostan, about 1,200 km east of Moscow, and drones reached the Omsk region in Siberia.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine said its forces struck a large oil refinery complex in the city of Salavat, some 1,200 kilometers (about 750 miles) east of Moscow ... Ukrainian drones also reached Russia's Omsk region in western Siberia

stories.headline: US suspends Microsoft, Adobe and six IT outsourcers from green-card sponsorship program

key_facts.fact: On October 8, the Trump administration suspended Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini from the PERM permanent labor certification program used for employment-based green cards.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft and software maker Adobe are among eight the companies that the Trump Administration will suspend from applying to sponsor employment-based green cards. The other companies are major information technology outsourcing firms: Cognizant; Infosys; Tata Consultancy Services; Wipro; HCL Technologies; and Capgemini.

key_facts.fact: Vice President JD Vance said Microsoft laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards.
key_facts.excerpt: He said the company laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B temporary worker visas and nearly 3,000 green cards.

key_facts.fact: Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said no new or pending permanent labor certification applications from these companies will be processed; he said they received over 230,000 H-1B approvals and 100,000+ labor certifications since 2009.
key_facts.excerpt: "We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," Sonderling said.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft said about 80% of its roughly 6,000 H-1B applications last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of existing employees, not new hires.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft ... said of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications it submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% were "to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees."

key_facts.fact: Vance said the suspensions would last 'as long as it needs to'; the administration also opened probes into nine universities, including Harvard, Yale and Stanford, over J-1 exchange visas.
key_facts.excerpt: Vance said the suspensions would last "as long as it needs to" ... Vance also said nine universities, including Harvard, Yale and Stanford, would be investigated

key_facts.fact: Microsoft is the largest filer of PERM applications according to Labor Department data through June 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Labor Department data through June 2026, Microsoft was the largest filer of applications via the PERM program

stories.headline: SpaceX buys Grain's nationwide 800 MHz spectrum for Starlink Mobile; AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile slide

key_facts.fact: On October 8, Grain Management announced a definitive agreement for SpaceX to acquire 100% of its nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio, subject to FCC approval.
key_facts.excerpt: Grain Management, LLC ("Grain") ... today announced a definitive agreement under which SpaceX will acquire 100% of Grain's nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio. The transaction is subject to FCC approval

key_facts.fact: SpaceX said the portfolio covers up to 14 MHz of paired 800 MHz spectrum and closes 'one of the key remaining technical gaps' for Starlink Mobile to become a major US mobile carrier.
key_facts.excerpt: "This prime low-band spectrum addresses one of the key remaining technical gaps that will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the US," SpaceX said.

key_facts.fact: Grain had bought the 800 MHz portfolio from T-Mobile in August 2026 for $2.9 billion in cash plus its 600 MHz licenses; SpaceX did not disclose its price.
key_facts.excerpt: That company sold the portfolio to Grain in August, receiving $2.9 billion in cash and Grain's 600 megahertz spectrum licenses. The price of SpaceX's purchase was not disclosed.

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal reported SpaceX agreed to pay $8 billion for the spectrum, according to the Times of India.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies have not disclosed the financial terms, although The Wall Street Journal reported that SpaceX had agreed to pay $8 billion for the spectrum.

key_facts.fact: In after-hours trading AT&T fell 7.9%, Verizon 7.2% and T-Mobile 7.5%, while SpaceX shares rose 1.1% to $162.49.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares in AT&T fell 7.9% to $22.90 in after-hours trading. Verizon shares dropped 7.2% and T-Mobile shares slid 7.5%. Meanwhile, shares in SpaceX rose 1.1% to $162.49.

key_facts.fact: The deal came a week after T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon formed a satellite direct-to-device joint venture that excluded Starlink; Musk called the acquisition a 'very big deal'.
key_facts.excerpt: Last week, T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon formed a joint venture "focused on expanding coverage in underserved areas," via satellite and direct-to-device (D2D) services, and Starlink was notably absent.

stories.headline: FDA approves Roche's Tecentriq plus chemo after surgery for stage III dMMR colon cancer

key_facts.fact: On October 8, 2026, the FDA approved atezolizumab (Tecentriq) with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin as adjuvant treatment for stage III mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) colon cancer in patients aged 2 and older.
key_facts.excerpt: On October 8, 2026, the Food and Drug Administration approved atezolizumab (Tecentriq, Genentech, Inc.) in combination with a fluoropyrimidine and oxaliplatin for the adjuvant treatment of adult and pediatric patients two years of age and older with Stage III mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) colon cancer.

key_facts.fact: The FDA also approved the subcutaneous Tecentriq Hybreza for the same use in patients 12 and older weighing at least 40 kg.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA also approved atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs (Tecentriq Hybreza, Genentech, Inc.) ... for ... patients 12 years of age and older who weigh 40 kg or greater with Stage III dMMR colon cancer.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase III ATOMIC study, adding Tecentriq to mFOLFOX6 chemotherapy cut the risk of recurrence or death by 50% versus chemo alone; 36-month disease-free survival was 86% vs 76%.
key_facts.excerpt: ATOMIC demonstrated that adding Tecentriq to modified (m)FOLFOX6 chemotherapy reduced the risk of disease recurrence or death by 50% ... The 36-month disease-free survival was 86% for Tecentriq combined with mFOLFOX6 compared with 76%

key_facts.fact: The approval is Tecentriq's twelfth US indication.
key_facts.excerpt: This approval marks the twelfth indication for Tecentriq in the US.

stories.headline: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 splashes down off Los Angeles after 237 days on the ISS

key_facts.fact: NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA's Sophie Adenot and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev splashed down in the Pacific off Los Angeles at 8:34 a.m. PDT on October 8.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev returned to Earth at 8:34 a.m. PDT.

key_facts.fact: During the 237-day mission the crew traveled more than 100 million miles and completed more than 3,792 orbits of Earth.
key_facts.excerpt: During their 237-day mission, the four crew members traveled more than 100 million miles and completed more than 3,792 orbits around Earth.

key_facts.fact: Meir has logged 440 total days in space, placing her in NASA's top 10 for cumulative days; the crew conducted four spacewalks.
key_facts.excerpt: Meir has logged 440 total days in space, placing her in NASA's Top 10 for cumulative days in space ... The crew also conducted four spacewalks during their nearly eight-month mission.

key_facts.fact: The crew had launched in February, hurrying to the station to replace an ailing colleague and his crew.
key_facts.excerpt: Four astronauts returned to Earth from the International Space Station on Thursday after hurrying there eight months ago to replace an ailing colleague and his crew.

key_facts.fact: NASA and SpaceX target October 13 for the CRS-35 cargo launch, carrying more than 6,300 pounds including the final set of ISS Roll-Out Solar Arrays.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA and SpaceX are targeting 6:33 a.m. EDT, Tuesday, Oct. 13, for the next launch to deliver science investigations, supplies, and equipment, including the final set of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays
